# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (domain-joined to LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero |

Grounded in: ARP (`10.8.15.133 -> 00:1c:bf:03:54:82`), DHCP option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` tied to the same MAC, NBNS name registrations for `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV`, and Kerberos `CNameString` values `desktop-h8alzbv$` / `plucero` sourced from 10.8.15.133.

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory, only the pcap.

Behavioral evidence points to a **JS-downloader loader consistent with the Latrodectus/IcedID family of malware-delivery kits** (fake-invoice lure → padded WScript-executed JS → BITS-fetched DLL payload → encrypted HTTP beacon on port 80 with a static spoofed User-Agent). Key behavioral markers:

1. Victim resolves `quote.checkfedexexp.com` and downloads a ZIP named `managements?...` (SHA256 `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5`).
2. The ZIP contains a single ~6.99 MB file, `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (SHA256 `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`), bulk-padded with megabytes of scraped, unrelated document text (visible strings from IPCC/OECD/MPI reference material) surrounding ~731 `eval` and ~815 `function` occurrences and a single `WScript` reference — a classic JS-downloader obfuscation/anti-sandbox technique.
3. Victim visits `business.checkfedexexp.com` over TLS (SNI observed), consistent with the loader's landing-page check-in.
4. ~35 seconds later, the host uses **Microsoft BITS/7.8** to HEAD then GET `hxxp://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`, retrieving a **PE32+ x86-64 DLL** (SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`).
5. Roughly 60 seconds after the DLL download, the host begins persistent GET/POST beaconing to `72.5.43.29:80 /` (path `/`, no query) — 308 requests over ~1820 seconds. All requests carry the static, malformed User-Agent `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` and an opaque base64-blob `Cookie` header; POST bodies are binary/encrypted, not plaintext HTTP form data.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — evidence: BITS download of the DLL payload (`/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`, HTTP 200), followed by 308 repeated GET/POST beacons to `/` with encrypted cookie/body content and a static spoofed IE6 User-Agent, over a ~30-minute window (frame times 135.9s–1962.0s relative).

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159) — served the malicious ZIP via `GET /managements?...`.
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70) — TLS SNI visited by the victim ~25s before the DLL download; part of the same fake-FedEx lure infrastructure.

**Malicious URL**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — HTTP GET returning the ZIP archive.
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS-fetched DLL payload.

**Transferred files / hashes**
| File | SHA256 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `managements` (ZIP archive) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Exported via `tshark --export-objects http` from stream to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside ZIP) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Extracted from the recovered ZIP |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | BITS GET/HEAD to 72.5.43.29, HTTP 200, `file` confirms PE32+ DLL x86-64 |

## Benign context (not indicators)
- Standard Windows/AD chatter: `ldap`, `kerberos`, `cldap`, DHCP, NBNS, LLMNR, mDNS to domain controller `10.8.15.4` / `win-jegjix7q9rs.lafontainebleu.org`.
- Microsoft/OS telemetry and CDN traffic: `msftconnecttest.com`, Windows Update (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), OCSP (`oneocsp.microsoft.com`), Bing/MSN/Office/Teams/OneDrive domains, `sb.scorecardresearch.com`.
- Adobe update check: `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `armmf.adobe.com` (`ProcessMAU.txt`).
- SSDP/mDNS local discovery (239.255.255.250, `_googlecast._tcp.local`).

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as user `plucero` on the LAFONTAINEBLEU domain, was infected via a fake FedEx-themed lure (`quote.checkfedexexp.com` / `business.checkfedexexp.com`) that delivered a ZIP containing a heavily padded, obfuscated JavaScript downloader (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`). The JavaScript used Windows BITS to retrieve a PE32+ DLL payload from a bare-IP host (72.5.43.29), which then established persistent encrypted HTTP beaconing to the same IP on port 80 using a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer User-Agent. The traffic pattern (padded JS downloader, BITS-staged DLL retrieval, encrypted cookie-based HTTP beacon) is consistent with a Latrodectus/IcedID-family loader; this is a behavioral assessment, as no signature/IDS data was available in the provided evidence.
